sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can introduce yourself, spell your name and give your contact details.
sessions.title: Nice To Meet You
sessions.objective: Practice the alphabet; learn to give and spell your name and family name.
sessions.can_do: You can say and spell your name and ask someone's name.
sessions.language_focus: Be (am/is) with names; What's...? question; letter names A–Z
sessions.pronunciation: Letter names in sound families (A-H-J-K / B-C-D-E-G-P-T-V / F-L-M-N-S-X-Z); pause between letters
sessions.task: Student is a new learner at a registration desk. Student gives and spells given and family name; tutor repeats the letters back to check. Student = new learner, Tutor = receptionist.
sessions.exit_task: Gives and spells own full name; at most one letter needs repair.
sessions.tutor_notes: Commonly confused letters: E/I, G/J, B/P, V/B. Teach "Again, please." Don't assume given/family name order is the same in every culture.
challenge: Say your name.
Spell your family name slowly.
Ask someone: "What's your name?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can introduce yourself, spell your name and give your contact details.
sessions.title: How Are You?
sessions.objective: Learn to say how you feel and ask others how they are.
sessions.can_do: You can say how you feel and ask how someone is.
sessions.language_focus: Be (I'm/you're) + feeling adjective; And you? as a return question
sessions.pronunciation: Rising-falling intonation on How are you?; stress on the feeling word
sessions.task: Two neighbors meet in the morning. Each greets, asks how the other is, answers, and returns the question. Student = neighbor, Tutor = neighbor.
sessions.exit_task: Greets, answers with a feeling word, and returns "And you?" without prompting.
sessions.tutor_notes: Learners often answer "Fine, thank you" only; push for one more real feeling using picture cards. Do not over-correct "I'm fine, and you?" as a unit.
challenge: Say how you feel today.
Ask someone how I am.
Say: "I'm tired. And you?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can introduce yourself, spell your name and give your contact details.
sessions.title: What Do You Do?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about your job and where you work.
sessions.can_do: You can say your job and where you work.
sessions.language_focus: Be + job; work in/at + place; What do you do?
sessions.pronunciation: Weak stress on a/an; word stress in job words (teacher, doctor)
sessions.task: Student interviews the tutor and then answers the same questions about their own job or study. Student = interviewer then interviewee, Tutor = new colleague.
sessions.exit_task: Gives own job (or student/not working) and place using I'm a ___ / I work in ___.
sessions.tutor_notes: Include students, parents at home, and people between jobs; avoid assuming everyone has paid work. Use job pictures and L1 word bank.
challenge: Say your job.
Say where you work or study.
Ask someone: "What do you do?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can introduce yourself, spell your name and give your contact details.
sessions.title: How Do I Contact You?
sessions.objective: Learn to share and ask for contact information (phone, email).
sessions.can_do: You can give and ask for a phone number and email address.
expressions: It's ali at gmail dot com.
sessions.language_focus: Numbers 0–9 in strings; at / dot / underscore; What's your...?
sessions.pronunciation: Say numbers in groups (3-3-4) with pauses; "oh" vs "zero"; stress on the last number in a group
sessions.task: Student signs up for a class and exchanges phone and email with the tutor, checking by repeating back. Student = new classmate, Tutor = classmate.
sessions.exit_task: Gives a phone number and email clearly and confirms the tutor's by repeating it back.
sessions.tutor_notes: Teens vs tens (13/30) and 5/9 confusion. Use a practice number, not the learner's real one, if privacy is a concern. Teach "at" and "dot" before the task.
challenge: Say your phone number in groups.
Spell your email address.
Ask someone for my email.

sessions.pronunciation: Recycle the pronunciation points from Lessons 1–4; the tutor picks the two the learner struggled with most.

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can talk about your family, their ages and jobs, and your pets.
sessions.title: What Is Your Brother's Name?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about family members' names.
sessions.can_do: You can say the names of your family members.
sessions.language_focus: his/her; my/your; 's possessive with names; have + number
sessions.pronunciation: /s/ /z/ /ɪz/ ending in names and plurals (sisters, brothers); stress in family words
sessions.task: Student introduces members of their family using photos or a family tree card while the tutor asks follow-up name questions. Student = presenter, Tutor = interested friend.
sessions.exit_task: Introduces at least three family members by relationship and name using his/her correctly.
sessions.tutor_notes: Sensitive topic: some learners have lost or are separated from family. Offer a fictional family card as an alternative. Check his/her confusion.
challenge: Say your mother's and father's names.
Tell a friend about one family member: "This is my ___."
Ask someone: "What's your sister's name?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can talk about your family, their ages and jobs, and your pets.
sessions.title: How Old Are You?
sessions.objective: Learn to ask and answer questions about age.
sessions.can_do: You can ask and say how old people are.
sessions.language_focus: Be + age; How old...?; numbers 1–100
sessions.pronunciation: Teens vs tens (-teen/-ty) stress; stress shift in thirteen/thirty
sessions.task: Student interviews the tutor and a family-photo card about ages, then answers the same questions. Student = interviewer/interviewee, Tutor = new friend.
sessions.exit_task: Asks and answers age questions for self and two other people with the correct -teen/-ty.
sessions.tutor_notes: Some cultures find age questions rude: teach that it's fine with children and in class. Use a number line to practice -teen vs -ty.
challenge: Say your age.
Say how old two family members are.
Ask someone: "How old are you?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can talk about your family, their ages and jobs, and your pets.
sessions.title: What Does She Do?
sessions.objective: Learn to describe other people's jobs.
sessions.can_do: You can say what other people do for work.
sessions.language_focus: he/she + be and + work(s); third-person -s; Where does he work?
sessions.pronunciation: -s ending /s/ /z/ in works/drives; sentence stress on job words
sessions.task: Student talks about the jobs of three people in a picture set (or own family) and answers the tutor's Where / What questions. Student = describer, Tutor = curious friend.
sessions.exit_task: Describes three people's jobs with the correct he/she and one third-person -s.
sessions.tutor_notes: Third-person -s will be missed often; do not stop the flow. Record two uncorrected examples and fix them at the end.
challenge: Say what your mother or father does.
Say what a friend does and where.
Ask someone: "What does she do?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can talk about your family, their ages and jobs, and your pets.
sessions.title: Do You Have a Pet?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about pets and ownership.
sessions.can_do: You can talk about pets and say what you have.
expressions: Yes, I do. I have a cat.
sessions.language_focus: Do you have...?; I have / I don't have; its
sessions.pronunciation: Short answers Yes, I do / No, I don't (falling tone); -s plural (cats, dogs)
sessions.task: Student is interviewed about pets and then interviews the tutor; non-owners talk about a pet they like. Student = pet owner or future owner, Tutor = pet-shop worker.
sessions.exit_task: Answers Do you have...? truthfully and asks one follow-up question about the pet's name or kind.
sessions.tutor_notes: Cultural note: attitudes to dogs and cats vary; keep it neutral. Allow "I want a ___" for learners without pets.
challenge: Say if you have a pet.
Say the name of a pet you know.
Ask someone: "Do you have a pet?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can talk about your family, their ages and jobs, and your pets.
sessions.title: Review (Lessons 6 - 9)
sessions.objective: Review and practice key phrases from Lessons 6–9.
sessions.can_do: Milestone: After this unit you can talk about your family, their ages and jobs, and your pets.
sessions.language_focus: his/her; Be + age; he/she + be and + work(s); Do you have...?
sessions.pronunciation: Recycle the pronunciation points from Lessons 6–9; the tutor picks the two the learner struggled with most.

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can describe the weather, say what food you like and talk about your day and week.
sessions.title: How Is the Weather?
sessions.objective: Learn to describe current weather conditions.
sessions.can_do: You can describe the weather right now.
sessions.language_focus: It's + weather adjective; What's the weather like?
sessions.pronunciation: focus on /w/ in weather/windy; stress on weather word
sessions.task: Two friends talk on the phone from different cities about today's weather. Student = friend in city A, Tutor = friend in city B.
sessions.exit_task: Describes today's weather with two details and asks the partner's weather.
sessions.tutor_notes: Learners may say "The weather is rain" instead of "It's raining"; model, don't lecture. Use weather icons and real forecast screenshot.
challenge: Say the weather today.
Say the weather in another city.
Ask someone: "What's the weather like?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can describe the weather, say what food you like and talk about your day and week.
sessions.title: What Foods Do You Like?
sessions.objective: Learn to express food preferences.
sessions.can_do: You can say what foods you like and don't like.
expressions: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
sessions.language_focus: like/don't like + noun; Do you like...?; uncountable and plural nouns without article
sessions.pronunciation: Final /s/ in likes; contrasting stress in I LIKE it / I DON'T like it
sessions.task: Student surveys the tutor about food likes using picture cards, then answers the same questions for themselves. Student = survey taker, Tutor = interviewee.
sessions.exit_task: Says at least three likes and two dislikes and asks two Do you like...? questions.
sessions.tutor_notes: Check dietary/religious restrictions: don't assume pork or alcohol is a "normal" example. Use halal/vegetarian-neutral pictures.
challenge: Say three foods you like.
Say one food you don't like.
Ask someone: "Do you like fish?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can describe the weather, say what food you like and talk about your day and week.
sessions.title: What Is Your Daily Routine?
sessions.objective: Learn to describe your everyday routine.
sessions.can_do: You can describe the things you do every day.
expressions: I go to bed at ten.
What do you do every day?
sessions.language_focus: Simple present I; sequencers first/then/after that; time with at
sessions.pronunciation: Linking "wake up", "go to"; stress on the verb in short phrases
sessions.task: Student describes a normal day using picture sequence cards in order; tutor asks "What time?". Student = speaker, Tutor = new roommate.
sessions.exit_task: Describes at least five daily actions in sequence with two times.
sessions.tutor_notes: Check the verb forms: "I go to work" not "I go work". Allow gestures. Use clock face cards.
challenge: Say three things you do in the morning.
Say what you do in the evening.
Tell a friend your day: first, then, after that.

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can describe the weather, say what food you like and talk about your day and week.
sessions.title: What Is Your Weekly Routine?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about weekly habits and schedules.
sessions.can_do: You can talk about your weekly schedule.
expressions: I go to class every Wednesday.
What do you do on Fridays?
sessions.language_focus: on + day; every + day; present simple; always/never (introductory)
sessions.pronunciation: Day names (Tuesday /ˈtuːzdeɪ/, Wednesday) stress on first syllable
sessions.task: Student and tutor compare weekly schedules using a blank calendar: each interviews the other and fills in the other's week. Student = interviewer, Tutor = new classmate.
sessions.exit_task: Gives activities for at least four days using on + day and asks two questions to fill in the partner's calendar.
sessions.tutor_notes: Some learners' weeks differ by culture (weekend days differ); accept and name them. Teach the silent letters in Wednesday.
challenge: Say what you do on Monday.
Say what you do at the weekend.
Ask someone: "What do you do on Friday?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can describe the weather, say what food you like and talk about your day and week.

sessions.language_focus: It's + weather adjective; like/don't like + noun; Simple present I; on + day
sessions.pronunciation: Recycle the pronunciation points from Lessons 11–14; the tutor picks the two the learner struggled with most.

Say three things you do in the morning.
Say what you do on Monday.

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can make polite requests, talk about hobbies and ask and tell the time.
sessions.title: What Would You Like?
sessions.objective: Learn to make polite requests and offers.
sessions.can_do: You can ask for things politely and offer something.
expressions: Can I have some water, please?
sessions.language_focus: Can I have...? / I'd like... / Would you like...?; some; please/thank you
sessions.pronunciation: Polite rising intonation on Would you like...?; reduced "I'd" /aɪd/
sessions.task: Student is a guest at a friend's house or a café customer: the host offers drinks and snacks; the guest requests and refuses politely. Student = guest, Tutor = host.
sessions.exit_task: Makes two polite requests and one offer and answers with Yes, please / No, thank you.
sessions.tutor_notes: Politeness is carried by tone as much as words; model flat vs polite. Don't overuse "I want" as it sounds blunt.
challenge: Ask for a glass of water.
Offer someone some tea: "Would you like...?"
Say no, thank you.

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can make polite requests, talk about hobbies and ask and tell the time.
sessions.title: What Does He Like Doing?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about other people's hobbies.
sessions.can_do: You can say what other people like doing.
sessions.language_focus: like + -ing; he/she/they; Does she like...? questions
sessions.pronunciation: Final -ing /ɪŋ/; third-person -s in likes
sessions.task: Student describes the hobbies of three people on picture cards and answers the tutor's questions about each. Student = describer, Tutor = curious friend.
sessions.exit_task: Describes the hobbies of three people using like + -ing and answers one Does she like...? question.
sessions.tutor_notes: Learners might say "likes play"; keep the -ing chunk. Accept "love/enjoy" later. Use hobby pictures.
challenge: Say what your friend likes doing.
Say what your mother likes doing.
Ask someone: "What does he like doing?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can make polite requests, talk about hobbies and ask and tell the time.
sessions.title: What Time Is It?
sessions.objective: Learn to ask and tell the time.
sessions.can_do: You can ask for and tell the time.
sessions.language_focus: It's + time; o'clock, half past, quarter past/to; at + time
sessions.pronunciation: Time numbers with stress on the minute word; weak "to" /tə/
sessions.task: Student is at a bus stop or school office, asks the time and schedule times, and answers the tutor's questions. Student = traveler, Tutor = person at the stop.
sessions.exit_task: Tells and asks the time at least four times using o'clock, half past, and quarter.
sessions.tutor_notes: Digital reading (3:45) vs "quarter to four" is a common gap. Practice with real clocks, then digital times.
challenge: Say the time on this clock.
Say what time you eat lunch.
Ask someone: "What time is it?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can make polite requests, talk about hobbies and ask and tell the time.
sessions.title: What Does She Do on the Weekend?
sessions.objective: Learn to describe weekend activities.
sessions.can_do: You can say what someone does on the weekend.
expressions: What does she do on the weekend?
sessions.language_focus: Simple present he/she/they; on the weekend; third-person -s and goes/does
sessions.pronunciation: /z/ ending in goes/does; linking "on the" weekend
sessions.task: Student describes a family's weekend from a picture strip and then talks about their own. Student = describer, Tutor = neighbor.
sessions.exit_task: Describes three weekend actions for someone else and two for themselves with correct -s.
sessions.tutor_notes: Common form: "He go". Mark but don't stop. Weekend activity may differ by culture or religion; respect.
challenge: Say what you do on Saturday.
Say what a friend does on Sunday.
Ask someone: "What do you do on the weekend?"

sessions.title: When Is Your Birthday?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about dates and birthdays.
sessions.can_do: You can say and ask about dates and birthdays.
sessions.language_focus: ordinal numbers (1st–31st); months; in + month / on + date
sessions.pronunciation: /θ/ in fourth/fifth/twelfth/month; stress on ordinal ending
sessions.task: Student creates a class birthday chart by asking the tutor and picture-cast classmates for birthdays. Student = organizer, Tutor = classmate.
sessions.exit_task: Says own birthday with correct ordinal and asks two people their birthdays.
sessions.tutor_notes: Some learners don't know exact birthdates or use different calendars; accept "I don't know" and use calendar. Teach month order and ordinals through a chart.
challenge: Say your birthday.
Say today's date.
Ask someone: "When is your birthday?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can say dates and birthdays and talk about what you can do and which sports you like.
sessions.title: What Can You Do?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about abilities using 'can'.
sessions.can_do: You can say what you can and can't do.
expressions: Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
sessions.language_focus: can/can't + base verb; Can you...? short answers
sessions.pronunciation: Weak /kən/ in can vs strong /kæn/ in short answer; the /t/ in can't
sessions.task: Student plays a job-interview-style "what can you do?" game: asks the tutor Can you...? and answers truthfully. Student = interviewer/interviewee, Tutor = partner.
sessions.exit_task: Says three can and two can't statements and asks at least two Can you...? questions.
sessions.tutor_notes: Can/can't confusion is common; stress can't and use a falling tone. Allow gestures and skills in home languages.
challenge: Say three things you can do.
Say one thing you can't do.
Ask someone: "Can you swim?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can say dates and birthdays and talk about what you can do and which sports you like.
sessions.title: What Is Your Favorite Season?
sessions.objective: Learn to express preferences about seasons.
sessions.can_do: You can say which season you like best and why.
expressions: I like spring because it's beautiful.
sessions.language_focus: favorite + noun; because (simple); weather adjectives
sessions.pronunciation: Final /s/ in seasons /ˈsiːzənz/; stress on SEA-son
sessions.task: Student chooses a favorite season using picture cards and explains with two reasons. Student = presenter, Tutor = friend.
sessions.exit_task: States a favorite season and gives one reason using because.
sessions.tutor_notes: Seasons differ by region: some have only wet/dry seasons; accept those. Don't force four seasons.
challenge: Say your favorite season.
Say the weather in that season.
Ask someone: "What's your favorite season?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can say dates and birthdays and talk about what you can do and which sports you like.
sessions.title: What Sports Do You Like?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about sports you like.
sessions.can_do: You can say what sports you like and how you play them.
sessions.language_focus: play + sport; like + sport/-ing; Do you play...?
sessions.pronunciation: Linking in "play tennis"; stress on sport word
sessions.task: Student interviews the tutor and a classmate card about sports they like and play, then answers. Student = sports reporter, Tutor = interviewee.
sessions.exit_task: Names two sports with like/play and asks two Do you play...? questions.
sessions.tutor_notes: Play/do/go with sports is a later point; teach only "play + ball sport" now. Respect gender/cultural differences in participation.
challenge: Say a sport you like.
Say when you play it.
Ask someone: "Do you play football?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can identify and describe people, their jobs and what they wear.
sessions.title: Who Is This?
sessions.objective: Learn to identify and describe people in photos.
sessions.can_do: You can say who people in photos are.
sessions.language_focus: This/that/these/those (singular this/that); he/she/they; Who is...?
sessions.pronunciation: Contrast /ð/ in this/that; stress on the relationship word
sessions.task: Student shows photos (own or card) to the tutor and says who each person is, adding one word about them. Student = photo owner, Tutor = visitor.
sessions.exit_task: Identifies four people in photos with name and relationship.
sessions.tutor_notes: Be careful with sensitive family photos; offer a stock photo set. Don't assume two-parent families.
challenge: Say who a person in a photo is.
Say a person's name and one thing about them.
Ask someone: "Who is this?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can identify and describe people, their jobs and what they wear.
sessions.title: What Does Your Aunt Do?
sessions.objective: Learn to describe relatives' occupations.
sessions.can_do: You can say what your relatives do.
expressions: My uncle works in a bank.
sessions.language_focus: Present simple he/she; doesn't (introduce); jobs
sessions.pronunciation: Third-person -s; the vowel in "work" /wɜːk/
sessions.task: Student asks the tutor about relatives' jobs and tells about their own using a family-tree card. Student = interviewer/answerer, Tutor = friend.
sessions.exit_task: Describes three relatives' jobs with correct he/she and one doesn't work/ doesn't statement.
sessions.tutor_notes: Possessive 's and relative vocabulary may need review from Lesson 6. Not all relatives are employed; accept retired, studying, at home.
challenge: Say what your uncle does.
Say what your cousin does.
Ask someone: "What does your aunt do?"

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can identify and describe people, their jobs and what they wear.
sessions.title: What Do You Like Wearing?
sessions.objective: Learn to talk about clothing preferences.
sessions.can_do: You can say what clothes you like wearing.
expressions: I wear a uniform to work.
sessions.language_focus: like + -ing; wear; color + noun; comfortable/nice adjectives
sessions.pronunciation: Syllable stress in comfortable (COMF-ta-ble); /s/ /z/ in clothes (often /kloʊz/)
sessions.task: Student describes outfits for work, home, and special occasions using clothing pictures; tutor asks Do you like...? Student = describer, Tutor = shopper friend.
sessions.exit_task: Names six clothing items with colors and says one like/don't like statement.
sessions.tutor_notes: Be sensitive to modesty norms and uniforms. Avoid asking for details that feel personal. Teach plural-only words (jeans, pants).
challenge: Say what you wear to work or school.
